item.title: The minimax value of outcome feedback in budget-constrained adaptive sampling
item.description: arXiv:2611.28252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether adaptivity improves estimation is a classical question in sequential design and information-based complexity. In practice, adaptive data collection can use two different kinds of information: process data on whether each contact succeeded, and the observed outcomes themselves. How much each kind is worth in the worst case under a hard budget has not been settled. We study this question for estimating a common Bernoulli mean through channels with unknown response probabilities and known costs, where failed contacts are charged and the budget must hold on every sample path. We compare static designs, designs that adapt to response indicators only, and fully adaptive designs, each with an arbitrary estimator. Our main theorem shows that when the costs are invariant under a group of channel permutations acting transitively on the nuisance parameter, outcome-adaptive allocation has zero minimax value: response-adaptive and fully adaptive designs have the same minimax risk, given by a one-dimensional optimization and attained by an explicit least-favourable prior and equalizer rule. For two contacts we obtain a closed-form criterion for when response feedback strictly improves on every static design. An unequal-cost example with a computer-certified exact saddle shows that the same conclusion can hold without symmetry, even though no product prior is least favourable there. A correlated prior shows that outcome feedback can still reduce Bayes risk, so the equivalence is genuinely minimax. In this idealized setting, the results support responsive survey designs that adapt to paradata but not to outcomes.
item.dc:creator: Shengye Tao

item.title: Tuning the false discovery rate in the closed eBH procedure
item.description: arXiv:2611.28708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The closed eBH procedure controls the false discovery rate under arbitrary dependence between the input e-values. It takes the target false discovery rate $\alpha$ as its input and outputs a rejection set $R$, the usual goal being to maximize its size $\left|R\right|$. This note discusses a modification of the closed eBH procedure that allows choosing the target false discovery rate post hoc: the rejection set and its level $\alpha$ can be chosen after seeing the data, and the expected ratio of the false discovery proportion to $\alpha$ is at most 1. We adapt Vovk and Wang's (2023) algorithm for computing discovery e-matrices to computing, in quadratic time, the frontier of achievable combinations $(\left|R\right|,\alpha)$ of the size of a rejection set $R$ and its level $\alpha$. The frontier allows us to compute an optimal rejection set in view of a given utility function $F$, $F(\left|R\right|,\alpha)\to\max$, striking a balance between the goals of reducing $\alpha$ and increasing $\left|R\right|$.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Vovk

item.title: Nonparametric estimation of a common marginal hazard function under censoring and spatio-temporal dependence
item.description: arXiv:2611.28953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article investigates the nonparametric estimation of a common pooled marginal hazard function from right-censored durations exhibiting spatio-temporal dependence. We propose two estimators based respectively on the Nadaraya-Watson method and the (k)-nearest neighbors (k)-NN) approach. Under assumptions of stationarity, regularity, non-informative censoring, and weak spatio-temporal dependence, we establish their pointwise and uniform convergence rates as well as their optimal asymptotic order. A simulation study compares their finite-sample performance. Two real-data applications with right censoring are considered: a multicenter clinical trial with 53.8 percent censoring and 1,746 geolocated and time-stamped requests submitted to New York City's 311 municipal service, of which 35.5 percent are censored. The empirical results illustrate the relevance of the proposed methods in the presence of spatial and temporal dependence.
item.dc:creator: Ibrahim Loudy, Kowir Pambo Bello, St\'ephane Bouka, Guy Martial Nkiet

item.title: Limit theorems for almost conditionally identically distributed random variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.28967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $\xi$-Almost Conditional Identically Distributed ($\xi$-a.c.i.d.) random variables are generalizations of conditional identically distributed (c.i.d.) and exchangeable ones. $\xi$-a.c.i.d. random variables arise naturally in applications in statistics, such as in recursive algorithms and heteroskedastic observations, and are parametrized by a sequence $\xi=(\xi_{n})_{n\geq 0}$ that quantifies departure from the c.i.d. property. In this work, we extend limit theorems for exchangeable and c.i.d. random variables to the more general setting of $\xi$-a.c.i.d. random variables. After proving a Strong Law of Large Numbers, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the asymptotic directing measure of the sequence to be absolutely continuous with respect to a given $\sigma$-finite measure. Then, under regularity assumptions on the parameter $\xi$, three different Central Limit Theorems for $\xi$-a.c.i.d. sequences are derived, involving the predictive, empirical and asymptotic directing distributions. These theorems have several statistical applications, including the construction of asymptotic credible intervals in Bayesian predictive inference.
item.dc:creator: Marco Battiston, Lorenzo Cappello

item.title: Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.29058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace \tau_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||\Lambda_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.
item.dc:creator: Yugo Nakayama

item.title: The broken-sample problem revisited II: Detecting hidden linear dependencies
item.description: arXiv:2611.29186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the detection problem for shuffled linear regression, in which the covariates and the responses are either independent or linearly related through a latent correspondence. Consider independent standard Gaussian covariates \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and scalar responses \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\). In a shuffled linear model, \(Y_i=\langle X_{\pi_*(i)},\beta_*\rangle+\sigma Z_i\), where both the permutation \(\pi_*\) and the regression coefficient $\beta_*$ are latent and $Z_i$'s are white Gaussian noise. The goal is to distinguish this model from one in which the covariates and responses are independent with the same marginal distribution. In the low-dimensional regime of $d \ll \frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$, we show that the detection threshold is given by $\sigma=o(1)$ for fixed $d$ and $\sigma^2 = \Theta(\frac{1}{d\log d})$ for growing $d$; both thresholds are achieved in nearly linear time using moment-based test statistics inspired by matched filters in signal processing. For higher dimensions, tests based on sliced Wasserstein distance succeed when $\sigma^2 = o(\frac{1}{(d\log d)^2})$, while the optimal threshold remains open. As a by-product, we show that the shuffled linear model exhibits an ``all-or-nothing'' phase transition for estimating $\beta_*$ at $\sigma^2\asymp \frac{1}{d\log d}$ in low dimensions. In particular, $\beta_*$ can be consistently estimated in nearly linear time, even when it is information-theoretically impossible to recover any positive fraction of the latent matching $\pi^*$.
item.dc:creator: Shuyang Gong, Yihong Wu, Jiaming Xu

item.title: A high-dimensional perspective of assortative mating: definition, dynamics, and limiting results
item.description: arXiv:2611.29703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assortative mating, or the systematic (dis)similarity of traits between mate pairs, has wide-ranging consequences. Chiefly, it modulates genetic variance in offspring due to the coupling of inherited trait-associated loci in parents. Over many generations, this buildup becomes appreciable at the trait level and may confound statistical genetics techniques, such as association analyses and heritability estimation. Theoretical characterisations of this effect are well-developed in the univariate case, where mates assort on a single trait pair. However, empirical studies increasingly show that assortment is not only multivariate, but high-dimensional, in that the correlation structure exhibited between mates cannot be represented by a single or few linear combinations of the constituent traits. In spite of this, the mathematical theory of assortment has not scaled with awareness of this fact. In this paper such a generalisation is developed. We begin by deriving sufficient conditions under which an estimator is invariant to assortment, followed by studying existence conditions and limiting behaviour of equilibria under assortment. Finally, univariate results involving trait heritability and consanguineal genetic correlation are generalised to the multivariate regime.
item.dc:creator: K\'ari Hlynsson

item.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with a Matern Kernel
item.description: arXiv:2611.29841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) provide a flexible framework for modeling complex dependence structures through a covariance function, or kernel, whose parameters determine the variability, correlation, and smoothness of the underlying process. The Mat\'ern kernel is among the most popular choices due to its flexibility in modeling different degrees of smoothness. Although the identifiability of Mat\'ern kernel parameters under fixed-domain asymptotics is completely understood, identifiability alone does not establish the consistency or asymptotic behavior of the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) routinely used in practice. In this paper, we address this gap by developing a sharp asymptotic theory for the joint MLE of Mat\'ern kernel parameters. Since parameter identifiability depends critically on the dimension of the observation domain, we characterize the estimable parameters and establish their convergence rates across different dimensions. We establish joint asymptotic normality and minimax optimality of the convergence rates. In addition, we establish asymptotically valid confidence regions for the estimable parameters. Our results accommodate irregular sampling designs and extend to sub-Gaussian measurement errors. Extensive simulation studies illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Ameer Qaqish, Sudipto Banerjee, Didong Li

item.title: How long must an honest confidence interval be after causal discovery? Benign and malignant weak edges
item.description: arXiv:2611.30256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After causal discovery, a confidence interval for a total effect valid uniformly over the model class must pay for structural uncertainty. We measure this price by the worst-case ratio of expected length to that of the efficient interval knowing the graph, for linear Gaussian models with a known superset of the adjacencies and k-triangle faithfulness. The global price is of order sqrt(n) once one edge can be malignant, so we study it locally, near a generic distribution with one edge absent. Our main result classifies this weak edge by Meek closures. It is benign if deleting it leaves the effect identifiable in the resulting MPDAG and Markov equivalent explanations agree; the local price is then bounded, and otherwise, for small k, of order sqrt(n). At benign edges the price is of order R+K, with R a ratio of efficient lengths and K a cross-model constant. It equals one, so that honesty is free, exactly when K = 0, generically decided by a d-separation. For two Markov classes it is determined within a factor 3.40, and its upper bound is approached without knowing the base point or the weak edge. A further graphical condition gives the rate uniformly in a second edge's margin.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqi Zhao

item.title: Skew-Symmetric Factor Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.28301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The paper introduces and analyzes a factor model for (real) skew-symmetric data, which arise naturally in directed flows and in pairwise comparisons used for rankings. Working within a signal-plus-noise framework, we analyze spectral inference and establish a BBP-type phase transition in signal strength. Under Gaussian noise, we derive joint eigenvalue fluctuation limits. Above the separation threshold, the estimated signal strength is asymptotically normal whenever the population strength has multiplicity one. For a general multiplicity $k$, the joint limiting fluctuations of the corresponding sample eigenvalues above the threshold are given by the eigenvalues of a scaled $k\times k$ Gaussian unitary ensemble matrix. The skew-symmetric structure induces paired eigenspaces, and we characterize the canonical angles between the population and sample eigenspaces. Below the threshold, the corresponding largest sample eigenvalue converges to the edge of the semicircle law, with fluctuations governed by the Tracy--Widom $F_2$ distribution, in contrast to the $F_1$ law familiar from real symmetric models. The approach is illustrated through financial and demographic applications.
item.dc:creator: Anna Bykhovskaya, Tomas Espana, Jianqing Fan

item.title: Geometric ergodicity of Gibbs samplers for linear mixed models with several heavy-tailed random-effect components and unknown tail parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.28413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear mixed models with heavy-tailed random effects are widely used for robust Bayesian analysis of longitudinal data. We study the three-block Gibbs sampler for such models when the random effects are split into several components, such as random intercepts and slopes, each with its own scale and its own scale mixture of normals, when the tail parameters have priors on finite grids and are drawn jointly with the latent weights, and when the random-effects design is rank deficient, as when some subjects contribute a single observation. We give sufficient conditions for geometric ergodicity that attribute the rank deficiency to the components that cause it, and show that, under conditions on the gamma priors on the precision parameters, they hold for Student-t and slash random effects with individual weights, any grid of tail parameters and any design. The result extends to random-effect vectors whose coordinates share a weight, for subject-specific designs with known shape matrices. It justifies Monte Carlo standard errors for regression coefficients, log-scales and posterior probabilities of the tail parameters. Simulations show that the scale and the tail parameter can mix much more slowly than the regression coefficients, and an analysis of beta-HCG data illustrates the methods.
item.dc:creator: Rolando de la Cruz, Nathalie Humeniy

item.title: Limit distributions and bootstrap for smooth adapted Wasserstein distances
item.description: arXiv:2611.28468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we provide limit theorems for the Gaussian-smoothed adapted Wasserstein distances. Let $\widehat{\mu}_n$ be the empirical measure of independent paths with law $\mu$ on $(\mathbb{R}^d)^T$. Let $P = \mu * \gamma_\sigma$ and $P_n = \widehat{\mu}_n * \gamma_\sigma$, where $\gamma_\sigma = N(0,\sigma^2 I_{dT})$ is a Gaussian measure with mean zero and covariance matrix $\sigma^2 I_{dT}$. We first assume that $\mu$ is compactly supported. For every $1 < p < \infty$ and fixed $d, T$, and $\sigma > 0$, we show that $\sqrt{n}\,\mathrm{AW}_p(P_n,P) \Rightarrow Q_{P,p}(G)^{1/p}$, where $G$ is the Gaussian limit of the density fluctuation and $Q_{P,p}$ is the minimum adapted $p$-energy for the linearized continuity equation. We prove full-path bootstrap consistency and the convergence of the first and $p$-th moments. The limit and the bootstrap hold for noncompact laws as well, for all $1 < p < \infty$ under appropriate tail and structural conditions. For two-sided bounded density perturbations of strongly log-concave laws, the bandwidth is not restricted for $1 < p \le 2$. For $p > 2$, we give sufficient tail conditions and provide a Gaussian counterexample where root-$n$ tightness fails for small bandwidths. Our proof is based on a two-endpoint local expansion of bicausal transport. As an application, we provide asymptotic error bounds for optimal stopping values under the smoothed model using the bootstrap quantiles.
item.dc:creator: Xiaozhen Wang

item.title: The Curved Exponential Family of Cylindrical Distributions: m-Projection, Curvature and a Test of the von Mises-Fisher Component
item.description: arXiv:2611.28598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cylindrical data pair a vector in R^d with a direction in S^(m-1). We study a family in which the direction is von Mises-Fisher and, given the direction, the vector is Gaussian with mean affine in it; this generalizes the Mardia-Sutton model. The family is a curved exponential family inside a regular family with Fisher-Bingham directions. We state necessary and sufficient conditions for the maximum-likelihood estimator to exist and be unique. The estimator is explicit except for one scalar root and is the m-projection (Kullback-Leibler projection) of the moment-matching member. Every moment it does not match is a function of one residual, the gap between the sample and fitted second moments of the direction. The squared length of this gap in the Fisher metric is the classical score test of von Mises-Fisher against Fisher-Bingham directions, due to Cox on the circle and extended by Mardia, Holmes and Kent. Specific here are this reading and the exact invariance of its law to the regression part. The exponential curvature lies only in the directions of the regression matrix. In closed form, the information lost on this matrix against the expected information is m-1 observations for uniform directions and (m+1)^2/(m-1) in the limit of high concentration; conditioning on the directions recovers it. Finite mixtures are identifiable. On buoy records the test rejects von Mises-Fisher directions, and generalized von Mises directions raise the held-out log-density by 0.45 nats per observation with one component.
item.dc:creator: Amine M. Aboussalah

item.title: Exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study exact almost sure scale for non-negative stochastic recursions whose conditional mean consists of a linear term and a signed adapted perturbation. The linear term determines a product normalization, but convergence after normalization does not ensure a strictly positive limit. Multiplying the state by the inverse of each deterministic contraction factor gives a contraction-adjusted state. On paths where this state tends to infinity, we prove that the logarithm of the normalized state differs from the cumulative relative perturbation by an almost surely convergent quantity. The assumptions control the effective step sizes, the quadratic positive relative perturbation, and the conditional quadratic variation of the relative martingale noise. If the positive perturbation is summable at the normalized scale, the normalized process converges to a finite non-negative limit; strict positivity is then equivalent to absolute summability of the relative perturbation. We also give criteria for divergence of the contraction-adjusted state, first-order comparisons, and counterexamples illustrating the role of the hypotheses. Harmonic step sizes yield exact power laws with strictly positive random coefficients. Applications include learning automata, urns with signed sampling bias, response-adaptive reinforcement, generalized Simon models with signed updates, branching processes in varying environments, and linear stochastic approximation with multiplicative noise.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Aletti, Irene Crimaldi, Andrea Ghiglietti

item.title: Perturbed QMC designs and reduced QMC strength
item.description: arXiv:2611.28831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small errors in sampling locations can change the convergence rate of a cubature rule. We study this effect for equal-weight integration on spheres and determine how accurately the nodes must be realized to retain optimal Sobolev rates. Under an average energy condition on the reference nodes, we establish sharp perturbation bounds and characterize how the decay of node errors affects quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) strength, which measures the smoothness range over which optimal rates hold. We identify when this strength is preserved and when it can decrease, and show that sufficiently slow decay of node errors can destroy all optimal Sobolev rates. For a reference rule with optimal convergence, we further establish a necessary and sufficient condition on node accuracy for retaining the optimal rate uniformly over all permitted perturbations. Numerical experiments with spherical designs, Fekete points, and Coulomb-energy points illustrate the different stability regimes.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Ning Wu

item.title: Censored Regression Models with Endogeneity: A Survey
item.description: arXiv:2611.28835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This survey article provides a comprehensive overview of methodologies developed to handle endogeneity in censored regression models. We emphasize their theoretical basis, and estimating methodologies. The paper summarizes the benefits and drawbacks of each technique and addresses expansions to nonlinear, panel, and high-dimensional settings, offering researchers practical assistance and identifying options for future methodological improvement in censored models with endogenous regressors.
item.dc:creator: Swati Shukla, Shalabh, Subhra Sankar Dhar

item.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.28848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.
item.dc:creator: Ning Ning

item.title: Robust Pair--Restricted Lipschitz Regression with Global--Local Transfer
item.description: arXiv:2611.28936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a robust pair-restricted Lipschitz regression framework for grouped longitudinal data represented as finite trajectories in a space equipped with a prescribed or learned pseudometric. For a fixed geometry, latent responses and a Lipschitz bound are estimated jointly through a convex optimisation problem with constraints imposed on selected trajectory pairs. We show that the choice of fidelity loss leads to different structural behaviour: Huber regularisation strictly reduces the pair-restricted Lipschitz seminorm whenever the exact interpolant has a finite positive seminorm, whereas $L^1$ fidelity can preserve exact interpolation below a data-dependent threshold. For grouped observations, global and local Lipschitz structures are combined while keeping group identity outside the trajectory geometry. The global component draws on observations from other groups, while the local component uses each group's history to account for group-specific behaviour. We also characterise when group-specific observations can be fitted exactly under a shared Lipschitz bound and establish a regularity bound for the combined predictor. We describe a computational implementation based on constraint generation and illustrate the framework through an application to longitudinal sow-production data.
item.dc:creator: Sergi Sanjuan, Enrique A. S\'anchez P\'erez, Roger Arnau

item.title: Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.29179v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study extensive-rank matrix denoising for rotationally invariant signals corrupted by i.i.d. non-Gaussian noise. To exploit both the signal spectrum and the entrywise noise prior, we consider an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that alternates between a rotationally invariant spectral estimator and an entrywise denoiser. At each OAMP iteration, we conjecture a high-dimensional Gaussian equivalence property: the entrywise module admits an effective additive scalar Gaussian channel, whereas the spectral module behaves as if corrupted by i.i.d. Gaussian noise of matching variance. Under this conjecture, we formulate a state evolution (SE) recursion for the effective noise variances of both modules. Numerical simulations confirm that the SE predictions closely track the empirical mean-square errors. For robust principal component analysis (PCA), we apply this OAMP algorithm and characterize its recovery phase diagram via SE. Numerical results show that OAMP achieves a larger recovery region than several existing methods.
item.dc:creator: Zhuohang He, Qun Chen, Junjie Ma, Haochuan Zhang, Xiaojun Yuan

item.title: Directed Hypergraphs: Tensor Representation, Embedding Modeling, and Community Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.29655v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Directed hypergraphs, in which each hyperedge connects a set of tail nodes to a set of head nodes, are the natural representation for many-to-many interactions in citation networks, metabolic pathways, and group communications. Despite their broad applicability, community detection for directed hypergraphs remains statistically underdeveloped: most existing methods either collapse hyperedges into pairwise edges, treat the two sides as interchangeable, or require the number of communities to be known. We propose a statistical framework for simultaneous embedding and community detection in nonuniform directed hypergraphs. The method allows each node to have distinct roles as a source and as a target, accommodates varying hyperedge sizes, and automatically determines the unknown numbers of communities on both sides, which need not be equal, through a fusion-penalized likelihood. We establish consistency of the estimated numbers of communities, exact recovery of both membership structures, and consistent probability tensor estimation. We further show that exact recovery is attainable without knowing the numbers of communities by a procedure that does not rely on any particular local solution, and we complement the upper bounds with a minimax lower bound for probability tensor estimation and a necessary condition for exact recovery. To ground the methodology, we construct the Cross-Statistics Citation Network, a new large-scale corpus linking Statistics with Biology, Computer Science, and Economics. Applying our method to this corpus reveals source and target roles of author communities in cross-field knowledge flow, and a pairwise representation of the same citations partly merges these roles.
item.dc:creator: Guojun Zhu, Haofei Wang, Mingyang Ren

item.title: Identifiability of infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2611.29836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The problem of identifiability of the mixing measure for a location-scale mixture of Gaussian distributions is considered. We give sufficient and necessary conditions on the compact support of the mixing measure on unknown location and scale parameters for which the mixing measure's uniqueness can be guaranteed. This is achieved by an analytic and probabilistic framework that characterizes the null space of the Gaussian mixing operator, a linear mapping that transforms a space of mixing measures with compact support into that of Gaussian mixture distributions. This framework exposes a fruitful connection between the infinite location-scale Gaussian mixtures and the exiting behavior of a space-time backward Brownian motion from a compact domain, as well as the nature of the support of the heat potential associated with such a stochastic process. As a consequence of this theory we obtain complete characterizations of identifiability for several natural classes of location-scale parameter sets in terms of their topological and geometric properties. Our theory also yields canonical and identifiable representations of infinite Gaussian mixtures with mixing support contained within enclosed boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Nhu N. Nguyen, XuanLong Nguyen

item.title: Cumulants, Partitions, and Generalizations of P\'olya's Characterization of the Normal Distribution
